rendered: The anode-free full cell, built with a presodiated pyrite cathode, reaches an energy density of ∼400 Wh/kg[1], calculated on the mass of the presodiated pyrite and the carbon nucleation layer. The paper gives the theoretical maximum for LIB technology as 387 Wh/kg[2]. So the full cell's value is only slightly above that theoretical LiCoO2/graphite ceiling. The paper also notes that this figure is well above recent sodium-ion full cells, which reach only ∼200 Wh/kg[3] with respect to active mass. The authors add that, assuming a 50%[4] packaging penalty[5], the cell still exceeds current LIB technology.
